# Purpose

This R Markdown file performs a complete GO semantic-similarity summarization of compareCluster-style enrichment results across subnetworks. It keeps the original broad heatmap workflow, then adds the corrected selective workflow that emphasizes subnetwork-specific representative GO themes.

The main outputs are:

1. A broad SN x representative GO heatmap using recurrent representative themes.
2. A corrected selective SN x representative GO heatmap using theme specificity.
3. A binary selective enrichment heatmap.
4. Diagnostic plots to decide how many themes to show.
5. Summary tables for representative themes, SN-level themes, and GO-to-theme mapping.
6. Optional rrvgo semantic heatmap/scatter plots.
7. Optional GO semantic network for one selected SN.

# User parameters

```{r parameters}
input_file <- params$input_file
input_sheet <- params$input_sheet
organism_db <- params$organism_db
ontology <- params$ontology
padj_cutoff <- params$padj_cutoff

# This was originally 75. More selective interpretation generally benefits from 40-75.
# Recommended starting point: 50.
top_n_per_SN <- params$top_n_per_SN

# This was originally 0.7. More specific representative themes generally use 0.8-0.9.
# Recommended starting point: 0.85.
rrvgo_threshold <- params$rrvgo_threshold

# Original broad heatmap setting retained below.
top_theme_number_broad <- params$top_theme_number_broad

# Corrected selective heatmap setting.
top_theme_number_selective <- params$top_theme_number_selective
min_SN_per_theme <- params$min_SN_per_theme
max_SN_per_theme <- params$max_SN_per_theme
min_max_signal <- params$min_max_signal

cap_neglog10 <- params$cap_neglog10
binary_signal_cutoff <- params$binary_signal_cutoff
semantic_method <- params$semantic_method

selected_SN_for_network <- params$selected_SN_for_network
selected_SN_top_terms_network <- params$selected_SN_top_terms_network
selected_SN_similarity_edge_cutoff <- params$selected_SN_similarity_edge_cutoff
relevance_boost <- params$relevance_boost

output_prefix <- paste0("GO_", ontology, "_rrvgo_SN")
```

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
ratio_to_numeric <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  slash_idx <- grepl("/", x)
  if (any(slash_idx)) {
    parts <- strsplit(x[slash_idx], "/")
    out[slash_idx] <- map_dbl(parts, function(z) {
      if (length(z) != 2) return(NA_real_)
      as.numeric(z[1]) / as.numeric(z[2])
    })
  }
  if (any(!slash_idx)) {
    out[!slash_idx] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x[!slash_idx]))
  }
  out
}

sn_numeric_order <- function(x) {
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(as.character(x), "[0-9]+"))
}

make_heatmap_matrix <- function(sn_theme_tbl, selected_themes_tbl) {
  sn_theme_tbl %>%
    semi_join(
      selected_themes_tbl,
      by = c("representative_GO", "representative_term")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      theme_label = paste0(representative_term, "\n", representative_GO)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Cluster, theme_label, max_neglog10_padj) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = theme_label,
      values_from = max_neglog10_padj,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    arrange(sn_numeric_order(Cluster)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("Cluster") %>%
    as.matrix()
}

plot_complex_heatmap <- function(
  heat_mat,
  file_pdf,
  title,
  cap_value = 50,
  row_fontsize = 7,
  column_fontsize = 7,
  width = 16,
  height = 12
) {
  heat_mat_capped <- pmin(heat_mat, cap_value)

  # FIX: breaks were hardcoded (0,3,6,10,20,cap_value), which produces a
  # non-monotonic (invalid) break vector whenever cap_value <= 20 -
  # colorRamp2() requires strictly increasing breaks and will error.
  # Breaks are now generated dynamically from cap_value so any parameter
  # combination is safe.
  n_breaks <- 6
  breaks <- unique(round(seq(0, cap_value, length.out = n_breaks)))
  if (length(breaks) < 2) breaks <- c(0, cap_value)
  palette_full <- c("white", "#f7fcf5", "#c7e9c0", "#74c476", "#238b45", "#00441b")
  pal <- colorRampPalette(palette_full)(length(breaks))

  col_fun <- circlize::colorRamp2(breaks, pal)

  pdf(file_pdf, width = width, height = height)
  ht <- Heatmap(
    heat_mat_capped,
    name = "-log10(FDR)",
    col = col_fun,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    show_row_names = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = row_fontsize),
    column_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = column_fontsize),
    column_names_rot = 45,
    column_title = title,
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
      title = "-log10(adj. p)",
      at = breaks,
      labels = c(as.character(breaks[-length(breaks)]), paste0(">=", cap_value))
    )
  )
  draw(ht)
  dev.off()
  #invisible(ht)
  draw(ht)
}
```

# Read enrichment results

```{r read_data}
# FIX: originally assumed .xlsx unconditionally. Detect extension so the
# same Rmd works if you export your table as .csv/.tsv instead, and fail
# with an informative message rather than a cryptic readxl error.
if (!file.exists(input_file)) {
  stop("input_file not found: ", input_file,
       "\nCheck the `input_file` parameter in the YAML header.")
}

ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(input_file))
go <- switch(
  ext,
  xlsx = readxl::read_excel(input_file, sheet = input_sheet),
  xls  = readxl::read_excel(input_file, sheet = input_sheet),
  csv  = readr::read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE),
  tsv  = readr::read_tsv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE),
  stop("Unsupported input_file extension: ", ext)
)

go <- go %>%
  mutate(
    Cluster = as.character(Cluster),
    ID = as.character(ID),
    Description = as.character(Description),
    pvalue = as.numeric(pvalue),
    p.adjust = as.numeric(p.adjust),
    qvalue = as.numeric(qvalue),
    Count = as.numeric(Count),
    FoldEnrichment = if ("FoldEnrichment" %in% colnames(.)) as.numeric(FoldEnrichment) else NA_real_,
    zScore = if ("zScore" %in% colnames(.)) as.numeric(zScore) else NA_real_,
    GeneRatio_value = ratio_to_numeric(GeneRatio),
    BgRatio_value = ratio_to_numeric(BgRatio),
    neglog10_padj = -log10(pmax(p.adjust, 1e-300))
  )

glimpse(go)

cat("Rows:", nrow(go), "\n")
cat("Subnetworks:", n_distinct(go$Cluster), "\n")
cat("Unique GO terms:", n_distinct(go$ID), "\n")
```

# Optional ontology annotation and filtering

If the file contains only BP terms, this section will keep BP terms. If the file contains BP/MF/CC mixed together, this section filters to the ontology selected in the YAML parameters.

```{r ontology_annotation}
go_ontology <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  GO.db,
  keys = unique(go$ID),
  columns = "ONTOLOGY",
  keytype = "GOID"
) %>%
  distinct(GOID, ONTOLOGY)

go <- go %>%
  left_join(go_ontology, by = c("ID" = "GOID"))

# FIX: flag GO IDs GO.db couldn't annotate (e.g. obsolete/retired terms)
# instead of letting them silently fail the ontology filter below with no
# record of how many were dropped or why.
n_unannotated <- sum(is.na(go$ONTOLOGY))
if (n_unannotated > 0) {
  message(n_unannotated, " rows have a GO ID not found in GO.db (likely ",
          "obsolete terms) and will be dropped from downstream analysis.")
}

go_sig <- go %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(ID),
    !is.na(p.adjust),
    p.adjust < padj_cutoff,
    ONTOLOGY == ontology
  )

cat("Significant rows after ontology filter:", nrow(go_sig), "\n")
cat("Significant subnetworks:", n_distinct(go_sig$Cluster), "\n")
cat("Significant unique GO terms:", n_distinct(go_sig$ID), "\n")
```

# Keep top N terms per subnetwork

This step is retained from the original workflow, but the default is changed to 50 for better selectivity. Increase to 75 if you want broader coverage.

```{r top_terms_per_SN}
go_top <- go_sig %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  arrange(p.adjust, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = top_n_per_SN) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Rows used for semantic reduction:", nrow(go_top), "\n")
cat("Subnetworks used:", n_distinct(go_top$Cluster), "\n")
cat("Unique GO terms used:", n_distinct(go_top$ID), "\n")
```

# Define GO term scores for representative-term selection

The original approach used only maximum `-log10(p.adjust)`. That can favor very significant but broad GO terms. This corrected code keeps the original score and also defines a specificity-aware score using both significance and enrichment magnitude.

```{r scores}
# Original score retained.
scores_original <- go_top %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarize(
    score_original = max(neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Corrected score: combines statistical strength and enrichment magnitude.
# FoldEnrichment is used if available. If not, GeneRatio_value is used.
scores_corrected <- go_top %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarize(
    max_neglog10_padj = max(neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_fold_enrichment = max(FoldEnrichment, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gene_ratio = max(GeneRatio_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_SN = n_distinct(Cluster),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    max_fold_enrichment = ifelse(is.infinite(max_fold_enrichment), NA_real_, max_fold_enrichment),
    max_gene_ratio = ifelse(is.infinite(max_gene_ratio), NA_real_, max_gene_ratio),
    score_corrected = case_when(
      !is.na(max_fold_enrichment) ~ max_neglog10_padj * log2(max_fold_enrichment + 1),
      !is.na(max_gene_ratio) ~ max_neglog10_padj * max_gene_ratio,
      TRUE ~ max_neglog10_padj
    )
  )

score_vec_original <- scores_original$score_original
names(score_vec_original) <- scores_original$ID

score_vec_corrected <- scores_corrected$score_corrected
names(score_vec_corrected) <- scores_corrected$ID

summary(scores_corrected$score_corrected)
```

# Calculate GO semantic similarity matrix

```{r calculate_similarity, cache=TRUE}
go_ids <- unique(go_top$ID)

# FIX/IMPROVEMENT: godata() and calculateSimMatrix() are the slowest steps
# in this pipeline and are deterministic given (ontology, organism_db,
# go_ids, method) - cache them to disk so re-knitting while you tune
# thresholds/filters downstream doesn't recompute semantic similarity
# every time. knitr `cache=TRUE` on the chunk also helps, but an explicit
# on-disk cache survives a fresh knitr cache directory too.
cache_file <- paste0(output_prefix, "_simMatrix_cache.rds")

cache_valid <- FALSE
if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  cached <- readRDS(cache_file)
  # Only reuse the cache if it was built from the exact same set of GO IDs.
  # Changing top_n_per_SN or padj_cutoff changes go_top -> go_ids, which
  # must invalidate the cache rather than silently reuse stale results.
  cache_valid <- setequal(rownames(cached$simMatrix), go_ids)
}

if (cache_valid) {
  semdata <- cached$semdata
  simMatrix <- cached$simMatrix
} else {
  semdata <- GOSemSim::godata(
    annoDb = organism_db,
    ont = ontology,
    keytype = "ENTREZID"
  )

  simMatrix <- rrvgo::calculateSimMatrix(
    go_ids,
    orgdb = organism_db,
    ont = ontology,
    method = semantic_method,
    semdata = semdata
  )

  saveRDS(list(semdata = semdata, simMatrix = simMatrix), cache_file)
}

dim(simMatrix)
```

# Compare semantic thresholds

This diagnostic helps determine whether `rrvgo_threshold` is too broad or too strict.

```{r threshold_diagnostic}
threshold_grid <- c(0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9)

threshold_summary <- map_dfr(threshold_grid, function(thr) {
  reduced_tmp <- rrvgo::reduceSimMatrix(
    simMatrix,
    scores = score_vec_corrected,
    threshold = thr,
    orgdb = organism_db
  )
  tibble(
    threshold = thr,
    n_input_GO_terms = nrow(reduced_tmp),
    n_representative_terms = n_distinct(reduced_tmp$parent),
    median_group_size = median(table(reduced_tmp$parent)),
    max_group_size = max(table(reduced_tmp$parent))
  )
})

threshold_summary

p_threshold <- ggplot(threshold_summary, aes(x = threshold, y = n_representative_terms)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = "Effect of rrvgo semantic similarity threshold",
    x = "rrvgo similarity threshold",
    y = "Number of representative GO terms"
  )

p_threshold

ggsave(
  paste0(output_prefix, "_threshold_diagnostic.pdf"),
  p_threshold,
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)
```

# Reduce redundant GO terms with rrvgo

This is the corrected reduction using `rrvgo_threshold` and the corrected score vector. The original style is retained but improved.

```{r reduce_terms}
reducedTerms <- rrvgo::reduceSimMatrix(
  simMatrix,
  scores = score_vec_corrected,
  threshold = rrvgo_threshold,
  orgdb = organism_db
)

reducedTerms_df <- reducedTerms %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("ID") %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ID,
    parent,
    term,
    parentTerm,
    score,
    size,
    everything()
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    representative_GO = parent,
    representative_term = parentTerm
  )

cat("Input GO terms:", n_distinct(go_top$ID), "\n")
cat("Representative parent terms:", n_distinct(reducedTerms_df$representative_GO), "\n")

head(reducedTerms_df)
```

# Map GO terms to representative semantic themes

```{r map_terms}
go_mapped <- go_top %>%
  left_join(
    reducedTerms_df %>%
      dplyr::select(ID, representative_GO, representative_term, term, score, size),
    by = "ID"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(representative_GO))

sn_theme <- go_mapped %>%
  group_by(Cluster, representative_GO, representative_term) %>%
  summarize(
    best_padj = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_neglog10_padj = max(neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_GO_terms = n_distinct(ID),
    total_gene_hits = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_fold_enrichment = max(FoldEnrichment, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gene_ratio = max(GeneRatio_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    example_terms = paste(head(unique(Description), 4), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    max_fold_enrichment = ifelse(is.infinite(max_fold_enrichment), NA_real_, max_fold_enrichment),
    max_gene_ratio = ifelse(is.infinite(max_gene_ratio), NA_real_, max_gene_ratio)
  )

head(sn_theme)
```

























# Theme metrics and selectivity diagnostics

This section is the major correction. Instead of choosing themes only because they occur in many SNs, this code calculates how selective each representative GO theme is across SNs.

A relevance boost is also applied here: themes whose wording matches a curated
set of cancer/brain-tumor biology keywords get their `selective_score`
multiplied by `relevance_boost` (default 1.6). This is a RE-RANKING WEIGHT,
not a filter -- every theme, matching or not, is still fully present in
`theme_metrics` and eligible for the broad/selective heatmaps. Matching
themes are simply more likely to rank inside the top N shown. Set
`relevance_boost: 1.0` in the YAML params to disable this entirely and fall
back to pure statistical selectivity.

```{r theme_metrics}
n_total_SN <- n_distinct(go_sig$Cluster)

# Edit this list to change what counts as "topic relevant." Matching uses
# word-boundary regex (case-insensitive substring matching on raw words would
# false-positive, e.g. unbounded "ras" matches inside "transferase").
topic_keywords <- c(
  "cell cycle", "mitotic", "proliferation", "apoptotic", "apoptosis",
  "senescence", "DNA damage", "DNA repair", "genome stability",
  "chromosome segregation", "telomere", "checkpoint", "spindle",
  "centromere", "kinetochore", "anaphase", "metaphase", "cyclin",
  "EGFR", "receptor tyrosine kinase", "MAPK cascade", "ERK1 and ERK2",
  "PI3K", "AKT", "TOR signaling", "mTOR", "ras GTPase",
  "ras protein signal transduction", "WNT signaling", "notch signaling",
  "transforming growth factor", "p53 class mediator", "RTK",
  "angiogenesis", "extracellular matrix", "cell migration", "cell adhesion",
  "invasion", "epithelial to mesenchymal", "hypoxia", "blood vessel",
  "immune response", "inflammatory response", "microglia", "cytokine",
  "glial", "glia", "neural stem cell", "neuron differentiation",
  "gliogenesis", "astrocyte", "oligodendrocyte", "blood-brain barrier",
  "blood brain barrier", "stem cell population", "autophagy", "stemness"
)
escape_regex <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "([.|()\\^\\$*+?{}\\[\\]\\\\])", "\\\\\\1")
topic_pattern <- paste0("\\b(", paste(escape_regex(topic_keywords), collapse = "|"), ")\\b")

theme_metrics <- sn_theme %>%
  group_by(representative_GO, representative_term) %>%
  summarize(
    n_SN = n_distinct(Cluster),
    max_signal = max(max_neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_signal = mean(max_neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_signal = median(max_neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_signal = sd(max_neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_GO_terms = sum(n_GO_terms, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_gene_hits = sum(total_gene_hits, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sd_signal = replace_na(sd_signal, 0),
    specificity_score = max_signal / (mean_signal + 0.1),
    variance_score = sd_signal,
    broadness_fraction = n_SN / n_total_SN,
    selective_score_raw = specificity_score * (variance_score + 0.1) / (broadness_fraction + 0.05),
    topic_relevant = str_detect(str_to_lower(representative_term), str_to_lower(topic_pattern)),
    relevance_multiplier = if_else(topic_relevant, relevance_boost, 1.0),
    selective_score = selective_score_raw * relevance_multiplier
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(selective_score))

cat("Themes matching topic keywords:", sum(theme_metrics$topic_relevant),
    "of", nrow(theme_metrics), "\n")

head(theme_metrics, 20)
```

# Original broad heatmap workflow retained

This retains the original logic: choose common/recurrent strong themes. This is useful as an overview but may look globally correlated because it intentionally favors themes that occur in many SNs.

```{r broad_themes}
top_themes_broad <- theme_metrics %>%
  arrange(desc(n_SN), desc(max_signal), desc(mean_signal)) %>%
  slice_head(n = top_theme_number_broad)

top_themes_broad

heat_mat_broad <- make_heatmap_matrix(sn_theme, top_themes_broad)

dim(heat_mat_broad)
```

```{r plot_broad_heatmap}
plot_complex_heatmap(
  heat_mat = heat_mat_broad,
  file_pdf = paste0(output_prefix, "_BROAD_top", top_theme_number_broad, "_heatmap.pdf"),
  title = paste0("Broad/recurrent representative GO themes, top ", top_theme_number_broad),
  cap_value = cap_neglog10,
  width = 16,
  height = 12
)
```

# Corrected selective representative-GO heatmap

This is the recommended main figure. It filters out near-universal representative GO terms and ranks the remaining terms by selectivity.

```{r selective_themes}
# Topic-relevant themes are exempt from the max_SN_per_theme UPPER bound only.
# Rationale: some genuinely strong, highly significant cancer/brain-tumor
# biology (e.g. apoptotic signaling, telomere maintenance) is so pervasive
# across SNs that the "selective" filter -- whose job is separating focused
# biology from universal housekeeping signal -- would otherwise exclude it
# for being "too common," even though max_signal shows it's real and strong.
# The minimum recurrence (min_SN_per_theme) and minimum significance
# (min_max_signal) floors still apply to topic-relevant themes exactly as
# they do to everything else -- this only relaxes the upper bound, and only
# for topic-matched themes. Set relevance_boost's effect here to "off" by
# making this exemption match topic_relevant == FALSE for everyone if you
# want the original symmetric window back.
selective_themes <- theme_metrics %>%
  filter(
    n_SN >= min_SN_per_theme,
    max_signal >= min_max_signal,
    n_SN <= max_SN_per_theme | topic_relevant
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(selective_score), desc(max_signal))

cat("Candidate selective themes:", nrow(selective_themes), "\n")
cat("  of which topic-relevant:", sum(selective_themes$topic_relevant),
    "(", sum(selective_themes$topic_relevant & selective_themes$n_SN > max_SN_per_theme),
    "included via the max_SN_per_theme exemption)\n")

if (nrow(selective_themes) < top_theme_number_selective) {
  warning("Fewer selective themes than top_theme_number_selective. Consider increasing max_SN_per_theme or lowering min_max_signal.")
}

top_themes_selective <- selective_themes %>%
  slice_head(n = top_theme_number_selective)

top_themes_selective

heat_mat_selective <- make_heatmap_matrix(sn_theme, top_themes_selective)

dim(heat_mat_selective)
```

```{r plot_selective_heatmap}
plot_complex_heatmap(
  heat_mat = heat_mat_selective,
  file_pdf = paste0(output_prefix, "_SELECTIVE_top", top_theme_number_selective, "_heatmap.pdf"),
  title = paste0(
    "Selective representative GO themes, top ", top_theme_number_selective,
    " | n_SN ", min_SN_per_theme, "-", max_SN_per_theme,
    " | max -log10(FDR) >= ", min_max_signal
  ),
  cap_value = cap_neglog10,
  width = 15,
  height = 12
)
```

# Binary selective enrichment heatmap

This version often looks cleaner because it asks whether a theme is strongly enriched or not, instead of letting extremely small FDR values dominate visual similarity.

```{r binary_heatmap}
binary_mat <- heat_mat_selective
binary_mat[binary_mat < binary_signal_cutoff] <- 0
binary_mat[binary_mat >= binary_signal_cutoff] <- 1

# FIX: ComplexHeatmap requires a discrete (character/factor) matrix when
# `col` is a named vector; a numeric 0/1 matrix + named-vector `col` errors
# or silently mis-colors depending on version. Convert explicitly.
binary_mat_char <- matrix(
  as.character(binary_mat),
  nrow = nrow(binary_mat),
  dimnames = dimnames(binary_mat)
)

pdf(
  paste0(output_prefix, "_SELECTIVE_binary_cutoff", binary_signal_cutoff, "_heatmap.pdf"),
  width = 15,
  height = 12
)

ht_binary <- Heatmap(
  binary_mat_char,
  name = "Strongly enriched",
  col = c("0" = "white", "1" = "#2166ac"),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 7),
  column_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 7),
  column_names_rot = 45,
  column_title = paste0(
    "Binary selective GO themes | 1 = -log10(FDR) >= ",
    binary_signal_cutoff
  )
)

draw(ht_binary)
dev.off()
draw(ht_binary)

```

# Optional row-normalized selective heatmap

This version highlights the strongest themes within each SN. It should not replace the FDR heatmap, but it is useful for visual pattern discovery.

```{r row_scaled_heatmap}
row_scaled_mat <- heat_mat_selective
row_scaled_mat <- t(scale(t(row_scaled_mat)))
row_scaled_mat[is.na(row_scaled_mat)] <- 0
row_scaled_mat[row_scaled_mat > 2.5] <- 2.5
row_scaled_mat[row_scaled_mat < -2.5] <- -2.5

pdf(
  paste0(output_prefix, "_SELECTIVE_rowZ_heatmap.pdf"),
  width = 15,
  height = 12
)

col_fun_z <- circlize::colorRamp2(
  c(-2.5, 0, 2.5),
  c("#2166ac", "white", "#b2182b")
)

ht_z <- Heatmap(
  row_scaled_mat,
  name = "Row z-score",
  col = col_fun_z,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 7),
  column_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 7),
  column_names_rot = 45,
  column_title = "Row-normalized selective GO themes"
)

draw(ht_z)
dev.off()
draw(ht_z)

```

# Optional semantic network for one SN

A DAG/network for all 92 SNs is usually too dense. This optional plot is for one selected SN.

```{r selected_SN_network}
terms_sn <- go_mapped %>%
  filter(Cluster == selected_SN_for_network) %>%
  arrange(p.adjust) %>%
  slice_head(n = selected_SN_top_terms_network)

ids_sn <- unique(terms_sn$ID)

if (length(ids_sn) >= 3) {
  sim_sn <- simMatrix[ids_sn, ids_sn, drop = FALSE]

  edge_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(sim_sn)) %>%
    dplyr::rename(from = Var1, to = Var2, similarity = Freq) %>%
    mutate(
      from = as.character(from),
      to = as.character(to)
    ) %>%
    filter(
      from != to,
      similarity >= selected_SN_similarity_edge_cutoff
    ) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(edge_id = paste(sort(c(from, to)), collapse = "__")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    distinct(edge_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::select(-edge_id)

  node_df <- terms_sn %>%
    distinct(ID, Description, p.adjust, representative_term) %>%
    mutate(
      neglog10_padj = -log10(pmax(p.adjust, 1e-300)),
      label = paste0(Description, "\n", ID)
    )

  g <- graph_from_data_frame(
    edge_df,
    vertices = node_df,
    directed = FALSE
  )

  p_network <- ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
    geom_edge_link(aes(width = similarity), alpha = 0.25, color = "gray50") +
    geom_node_point(aes(size = neglog10_padj, color = representative_term), alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = Description), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
    scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2)) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "right") +
    ggtitle(paste0(selected_SN_for_network, " GO semantic similarity network"))

  p_network

  ggsave(
    paste0(output_prefix, "_", selected_SN_for_network, "_semantic_network.pdf"),
    p_network,
    width = 12,
    height = 10
  )
} else {
  message("Not enough GO terms for selected SN network plot.")
}
```

# Export summary tables

```{r export_tables}
sn_top10_themes <- sn_theme %>%
  arrange(Cluster, best_padj) %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  ungroup()

sn_stats <- go_sig %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  summarize(
    n_significant_GO = n_distinct(ID),
    best_padj = min(p.adjust, na.rm = TRUE),
    strongest_signal = max(neglog10_padj, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_hits = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(sn_numeric_order(Cluster))

go_to_theme_map <- go_mapped %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Cluster,
    ID,
    Description,
    representative_GO,
    representative_term,
    p.adjust,
    neglog10_padj,
    FoldEnrichment,
    GeneRatio,
    GeneRatio_value,
    Count,
    GeneNames
  ) %>%
  arrange(Cluster, representative_term, p.adjust)

heatmap_matrix_broad_tbl <- heat_mat_broad %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Cluster")

heatmap_matrix_selective_tbl <- heat_mat_selective %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Cluster")

binary_matrix_selective_tbl <- binary_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Cluster")

output_xlsx <- paste0(output_prefix, "_semantic_theme_summary_FULL.xlsx")

writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    README = tibble(
      item = c(
        "input_file",
        "ontology",
        "padj_cutoff",
        "top_n_per_SN",
        "rrvgo_threshold",
        "semantic_method",
        "broad_top_theme_number",
        "selective_top_theme_number",
        "selective_min_SN_per_theme",
        "selective_max_SN_per_theme",
        "selective_min_max_signal",
        "binary_signal_cutoff",
        "main_recommended_figure"
      ),
      value = c(
        input_file,
        ontology,
        padj_cutoff,
        top_n_per_SN,
        rrvgo_threshold,
        semantic_method,
        top_theme_number_broad,
        top_theme_number_selective,
        min_SN_per_theme,
        max_SN_per_theme,
        min_max_signal,
        binary_signal_cutoff,
        paste0(output_prefix, "_SELECTIVE_top", top_theme_number_selective, "_heatmap.pdf")
      )
    ),
    SN_stats = sn_stats,
    Theme_metrics_all = theme_metrics,
    Top_themes_broad = top_themes_broad,
    Top_themes_selective = top_themes_selective,
    SN_theme_all = sn_theme,
    SN_top10_themes = sn_top10_themes,
    GO_to_theme_map = go_to_theme_map,
    Heatmap_matrix_broad = heatmap_matrix_broad_tbl,
    Heatmap_matrix_selective = heatmap_matrix_selective_tbl,
    Binary_matrix_selective = binary_matrix_selective_tbl,
    RRVGO_reduced_terms = reducedTerms_df,
    Threshold_diagnostic = threshold_summary
  ),
  path = output_xlsx
)

cat("Wrote:", output_xlsx, "\n")
```

# Recommended interpretation

For your main figure, use the file ending in:

```{r final_file_names, results='asis'}
cat("\n")
cat("Recommended main heatmap PDF: ", paste0(output_prefix, "_SELECTIVE_top", top_theme_number_selective, "_heatmap.pdf"), "\n")
cat("Recommended binary heatmap PDF: ", paste0(output_prefix, "_SELECTIVE_binary_cutoff", binary_signal_cutoff, "_heatmap.pdf"), "\n")
cat("Supplemental broad heatmap PDF: ", paste0(output_prefix, "_BROAD_top", top_theme_number_broad, "_heatmap.pdf"), "\n")
cat("Summary workbook: ", output_xlsx, "\n")
```

The broad heatmap is useful for showing global biological programs shared across subnetworks. The selective heatmap is better for identifying representative GO themes that distinguish subnetworks from each other.
